results.name: A01 accepted forms: @name, name, x.com / twitter.com URLs (incl. www, mobile, trailing path/query), numeric id, /i/user/<id>, intent/user?user_id=
A02 rejected: reserved product paths, other hosts / look-alikes, credentials, ports, other schemes, malformed names, empty / oversize / non-strings
A03 "@123" is a USERNAME (all-digit names exist) while a bare "123" is an id; a URL path of digits is a username; digit strings that are not valid ids ("0", leading zero) can only be usernames
A04 ids stay strings (no Number() anywhere): a 20-digit id parses exactly
A05 userOf: id must be a STRING of the id shape; numbers (already lossy), leading zeros, blanks are refused
A06 userOf display metadata is sanitised: non-https avatar dropped, bad username blanked, non-integer / negative / string follower counts become null
B01 RFC 7636 Appendix B vector: S256 challenge of the sample verifier
B02 derived verifier: 43 unreserved chars (RFC 7636), deterministic per state, different per state, different per secret, never the state or its hash
B03 deriveVerifier refuses a weak secret or empty state
B04 authorize URL: x.com/i/oauth2/authorize, code flow, exact client id + redirect URI, PKCE S256 with the derived challenge, our state, and NOTHING else
B05 the ONLY scope requested is users.read: no tweet.read, no offline.access
B06 authUrl refuses a missing / malformed challenge (never "plain", never absent) and an unconfigured client
C01 token exchange: POST api.x.com/2/oauth2/token, form-encoded, confidential-client Basic auth, code + grant_type + EXACT redirect_uri + code_verifier
C02 the client secret travels ONLY in the Basic header (never in the body, query or URL)
C03 GET api.x.com/2/users/me with the USER token as Bearer, asking for id,name,username,profile_image_url,public_metrics,protected
C04 an id above 2^53 survives as an exact STRING end to end (not rounded, not a number)
C05 a wrong PKCE verifier is rejected by X (the code is bound to the challenge) -> fixed code "denied"
C06 a different redirect URI is rejected by X (exact match) -> "denied"
C07 a grant without users.read is refused ("scope"); extra scopes do not widen what we request or keep
C08 a refresh_token (never requested) is ignored: only the access token string is returned
C09 an authorization code is single-use at X; reuse -> "denied"
C10 bad client credentials -> "denied"; missing config / malformed code / malformed verifier are refused before any request
C11 /users/me: numeric ids, bad ids, missing / odd "data", non-JSON, errors-only -> XError "malformed" (never an identity)
C12 /users/me with no token or a rejected token fails closed
C13 resolve: username / URL / id -> the immutable numeric id as a string + current display metadata; app-only Bearer; username lookup path /2/users/by/username/<name>
C14 resolve: unknown account (errors, no data) -> null; unparseable / reserved input -> null with NO request
C15 resolve: an answer for a DIFFERENT username / id than asked is malformed (fail closed)
C16 usersById: ids filtered / de-duplicated before the request, capped at 100, Map keyed by exact string id, public_metrics requested; unknown ids are simply absent
C17 usersById sends at most 100 ids per request
C18 usersById: malformed members are dropped, ids we did not ask for are dropped, "data" that is not a list or an answer with neither data nor errors -> malformed
C19 429 -> rate_limited (with Retry-After), 5xx -> unavailable, a hung request is aborted by the hard timeout -> unavailable; nothing retried
C20 no app-only bearer configured -> not_configured (no request made)
D01 creator-link platform=x returns the X start URL and scope users.read; the state is bound to platform x
D02 start -> 302 to x.com authorize with PKCE S256 whose challenge derives from THIS state (verifier never leaves the server), exact redirect URI, users.read only

D03 callback -> 302 to the FIXED creator page with a session fragment; a browser-supplied code_verifier / redirect_uri / redirect / next / returnTo is ignored (X verified the SERVER-derived verifier and the configured redirect)
D04 the creator session is bound to (x, numeric externalId as an exact string, wallet) from the AUTHENTICATED /2/users/me; subject spelling x_<id>~<wallet>

D05 link record: platform x, channelId (v1 name of the external id) = the numeric id string, wallet, display metadata, follower count read at that moment, scope users.read; NO username as identity field
D06 NOTHING secret is persisted, logged or returned: no access token, client secret, bearer, authorization code or PKCE verifier appears in the store, the logs or any response body
D07 exactly one token exchange and one /users/me per login; the discarded token is never reused
D08 the state is SINGLE USE: replaying the same callback -> #e=state and no provider call
D09 the consumed state nonce is recorded (atomic single-use marker)
D10 a YouTube-bound state is refused by the X function (start and callback): #e=state, no provider call
D11 and an X-bound state is refused by the YouTube function
D12 a tampered state is refused (start and callback)
D13 an expired state (10 min TTL preserved) is refused and X is not called
D14 missing code/state -> #e=state; provider error=access_denied -> #e=denied; neither calls X
D15 provider failures and malformed answers fail closed with FIXED codes (no detail leaks); no session is issued
D16 every outcome above redirected only to the fixed creator page (no open redirect)
D17 logs across the whole OAuth section never contain a token, the secret, the bearer, a code or a verifier (only hashed ids and fixed codes)
D18 per-IP limits are preserved on the X function (5 / minute)
D19 global daily budget: the (N+1)th login in a day is refused BEFORE any API call and WITHOUT consuming its single-use state
E01 @username -> immutable numeric id (string) + current display metadata; username is NOT part of the identity fields
E02 username / x.com URL / twitter.com URL / numeric id all resolve to the same immutable id
E03 cache: the same account (any spelling of the username) is served from cache with no new API call; the id spelling is cached separately
E04 cache entries are keyed by a hash of the normalised input and hold {externalId, title, handle, avatarUrl} for 1 h only
E05 reserved / non-user paths and junk input -> 400, and X is NOT called
E06 unknown account -> 404 (a miss is not cached, never invented)
E07 the platform parameter decides: platform=x never reaches the YouTube resolver
E08 malformed / mismatched API answers fail closed -> 503, nothing cached, no identity returned
E09 X outage / X rate limit -> 503 "could not be reached", nothing cached
E10 per-IP limits are preserved (20 / minute): the 21st request from one IP is 429
E11 spend guard (hourly): once the allowance of API requests is used, a NEW lookup is refused with 429 BEFORE any X request, while cached answers keep working
E12 spend guard (daily): the daily allowance holds across the hour windows and resets with the UTC day
E13 the shipped defaults are conservative request counts (not currency), and the guard is shared with OAuth / snapshots through one daily bucket family
E14 X resolver is CLOSED without the flag (400, no API call); the YouTube resolver builds its client from the environment and works (legacy `yt` and platform=youtube&q), with and without X enabled

F01 an X creator activates through the real OAuth link: manifest (platform x, channelId = numeric id string) accepted, creator record + public view carry platform x / externalId; no legacy channelId on the public view
F02 the creator-identity attestation names platform x and the numeric id as `externalId`, method x-oauth2-pkce users.read; no username / handle in it
F03 join-day snapshot (from the OAuth link): kind followers, platform x, numeric externalId, follower count, time, source - and NO handleThen / handle / title / avatar / channelId / subscriberCount
F04 a YouTube creator activates in the same deployment, unchanged
F05 daily job: ONE batch call to GET /2/users, an X snapshot with the dated follower count; YouTube snapshotted by its own adapter in the same run; per-platform report
F06 first success of the UTC day wins: a later run (and a changed count) never replaces it and does not even call X again
F07 no backfill: only the join day and the days the job actually ran exist (the skipped days between are absent)

F08 an X receipt is a normal v1 receipt: FINALIZED, creator manifest typed data platform x + channelId = numeric id string, and the EXISTING independent verifier returns RECEIPT VERIFIED (no receipt v2)
F09 the receipt context uses the transfer day's snapshot as dated FOLLOWER context; the line reads "Followers on X then: ~12K" - never the generic "Audience then"
F10 the receipt carries the identity + manifest + audience-snapshot attestations; the snapshot attestation is the follower one
F11 the public card: platform x identity in separate fields (no legacy creatorChannelId), follower context kind, still private by default
F12 X outage: no X snapshot is recorded, the failure is counted for X only, and the YouTube creator in the SAME run is still snapshotted
F13 a receipt for a day with no X snapshot reads "Followers on X then: unavailable" (kind kept, nothing guessed) and still verifies
F14 the outage is retried within the day and the first X success of that day is then THE snapshot (receipts of that day read it)
F15 a user returned WITHOUT a follower count records nothing (no guess) and is a counted failure; the other user in the batch is still recorded; the 20-digit id is exact
F16 an API answer with numeric ids is malformed: nothing recorded, counted as failure, the job still completes
F17 spend guard in the job: failing hourly retries stop calling X once the daily request allowance is used (2 attempts, then none), and the run reports budgetExhausted
F18 the allowance resets with the UTC day and the job resumes
F19 with the flag absent or false the job makes NO X request, records nothing for X and does not count X creators as failures (skipped)
G01 credentials + redirect present but the flag ABSENT -> X is closed
G02 flag false / empty / 0 / 1 / yes / "true " variants: only a (case-insensitive, trimmed) "true" opens X
G03 flag true + the complete configuration -> X is enabled, with OAuth and the resolver available; YouTube unchanged
G04 flag true but ANY ONE required value missing (client id, client secret, bearer, redirect) -> X is closed, and the cause names only the variable, never a value
G05 the redirect must be an https URL ending exactly in /api/early-x-auth (no http, query, fragment, trailing slash, other path)
G06 the YouTube configuration is independent of X: YouTube enabled/oauth/resolver identical with X absent, closed or open
G07 EARLY itself closed (no SYNCNET_EARLY_ENABLED) keeps everything closed regardless of the X flag

G08 with X closed (flag absent / false / a credential missing) EVERY X entry point fails closed: creator-link, resolver, creator view, Count me in, OAuth start + callback, X creator sessions, config; no X request, nothing stored
G09 YouTube is unaffected in every X configuration: Count me in, creator-link (YouTube start URL) and creator views behave identically with X absent, closed, half-configured and open
G10 config view with X open lists x with oauth+resolver availability and exposes no credential, secret, client id or redirect
G11 the EARLY kill switches close the X OAuth function too (writes disabled / EARLY disabled)
G12 without a strong session secret the X OAuth function answers unavailable (no PKCE can be derived)
G13 non-GET methods are refused; only the two documented GET shapes exist
H01 the X modules never log token / secret / code / verifier / bearer / authorization / state values (only fixed error codes, hashed ids and counters), and never use console.*
H02 the OAuth function stores only the link record (no token field) and never writes the client secret, bearer or verifier to the store
H03 X credentials / env names / hosts appear only in the config, adapter, platform-registry and X OAuth modules - not in the shared server code or the protocol lib
H04 the HTML pages contain no X markup or copy at all (X UI is created by script only when the server enables X; see tests/e2e/early-ui-x.mjs); the scripts never name the OAuth function or an X host
H05 the protocol and the verifier are untouched by X: domain, types, schema strings, matching rule
